nodes.description: Expressive language is the most severely affected developmental domain, and impaired language is one of the three features named in the disorder's own designation. nodes.description: The initiating lesion is a pair of NARS1 alleles, in trans, that reduce but do not abolish asparaginyl-tRNA synthetase function. Reported recessive alleles include missense changes in the unique N-terminal extension (UNE-N) domain (p.Thr17Met), in the catalytic domain (p.Asp356Ala, the recurrent p.Arg545Cys), and frameshift alleles (p.Met69AspfsTer4, p.Arg386ThrfsTer19). Complete loss of the enzyme is not compatible with life, so disease-causing biallelic genotypes are necessarily partial-function rather than null. Structural modelling of p.Arg545Cys predicts weaker spatial positioning and reduced tRNA selectivity through local destabilisation near the N-terminal end of the catalytic domain.

nodes.description: The convergence of the cortical and peripheral arms produces the clinical entity: global developmental delay and impaired intellectual development with poor or absent language, progressive microcephaly, delayed walking with an ataxic and/or spastic gait, seizures, and — where the peripheral arm is present — distal weakness and abnormal nerve conduction. Muscle tone may be low or high in different individuals, which is why the gait abnormality has no single characteristic form.

nodes.description: Cortical organoids differentiated from induced pluripotent stem cells of two affected individuals and two unaffected relatives from the founding biallelic families. At 28 days in vitro the organoids are indistinguishable; by day 52 the patient organoids are visibly smaller, and by day 90 none exceed 5 mm whereas almost all control organoids do. Daily monitoring excluded shrinkage — patient organoids simply never grow. This is the flagship human model of the disorder and the reason the microcephaly can be attributed to a progenitor-proliferation defect rather than to postnatal degeneration alone.

nodes.description: A subset of affected individuals develop a peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy, demyelinating or axonal, with atrophy predominantly of the distal lower limbs. Nerve conduction studies can be abnormal in early childhood. Peripheral nerve is a second high-demand compartment for the same reason as the cortex — long axons and myelinating Schwann cells sustain heavy biosynthetic loads — and its involvement is what makes NARS1 disease a combined CNS/PNS disorder rather than a pure microcephaly syndrome. The peripheral arm is not universal in the recessive form and is here modelled as a parallel consequence of the same translational shortfall, not as a downstream effect of the cortical defect.

nodes.description: The depleted progenitor pool yields a small cortex, and the ongoing translational insufficiency in post-mitotic neurons superimposes a degenerative component on the developmental deficit. Brain MRI in affected individuals shows severe microcephaly with diffuse cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, loss of both grey and white matter volume, and ventriculomegaly, with milder cortical and cerebellar atrophy on scans obtained earlier in the course — the imaging signature of a process that continues after birth rather than a fixed malformation.

nodes.description: The developing cortical neuroepithelium is the tissue least able to tolerate a translational shortfall, because radial glial cells must sustain a very high biosynthetic rate through repeated rounds of division. In patient-derived cortical brain organoids, DNA synthesis is reduced, SOX2-positive neural rosettes are fewer, smaller and poorly organised, and the mature-neuron marker TUJ1 is depleted, indicating failed generation of radial glia and consequent loss of the post-mitotic neuronal output pool. Single-cell profiling shows the astrocytic and radial glial lineages are both altered.

nodes.description: NARS1 is the sole enzyme that charges asparagine onto cytoplasmic tRNA-Asn. Patient fibroblasts and induced neural progenitor cells carry roughly half the normal amount of NARS1 protein and about half the normal tRNA-charging activity, and overexpression of the patient missense alleles shows the mutant proteins are unstable. The defect is specific: charging activity of the arginyl-, lysyl- and threonyl-tRNA synthetases is unaffected in the same cells, so this is not a general collapse of the translational apparatus but a targeted shortfall in one aminoacylation reaction.
